text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH 5xx rate detected for inference-gateway-eu (eu-west1) — 502 spike > 4% over 2m window. Escalation policy: inference-svc -> oncall -> level2 if unacked in 5m

pagerduty: Incident 3a7f9c - Acknowledgement required

devon: acked the pager. I'm looking. Seeing spike started at 2276543100, ramped quickly.

priya: same, watching k8s metrics now. Noticed a surge in upstream timeouts from origin-cache instances.

ops-sre: quick check — autoscaler hasn't kicked beyond base replicas because CPU spike is short-lived. Pod restarts are low. 502s look like upstream gateway timeouts (502 from origin pools) rather than model nodes OOM.

emma-li: pulling logs from gateway-ingress (eu-west1)

```
kubectl -n infra logs gateway-ingress-7b9f -c proxy | grep "502" | tail -n 30
[2026-03-14T02:45:03Z] 10.12.3.9 "POST /v1/generate" 502 342ms
[2026-03-14T02:45:13Z] 10.12.3.9 "POST /v1/generate" 502 410ms
[2026-03-14T02:45:28Z] upstream: connection reset by peer
```

sam-k: any recent deploys?

devon: there was a small config change 10m ago enabling a new cache-prefix eviction policy for embeddings cache. It increased origin fetches during warmup. Rolling back that change is my #1 candidate.

priya: confirmed: metrics show origin request rate ×6 for the embedding-cache service in eu-west1 since 2276543085. Replica CPU steady, but connection queue on origin spikes.

devon: mitigation plan: 1) throttled new cache policy (flip flag) 2) increase gateway concurrency limit and bump autoscaler min to handle transient load 3) temporarily route traffic from eu-west1 to eu-west2 for non-low-latency customers. I'll run 1 & 2 now.

ops-sre: I can handle the routing change if needed. Are we ok with cross-region latency for some traffic?

emma-li: customer impact: approx 2.1% of overall requests hit 502s in the EU cluster; a handful of customers (3 known mid-market tenants) reported errors via Sentry. No broad client outages reported. No SLO breach yet but error budget burn accelerating.

pagerduty: Acknowledged by devon at 2276543224

devon: flipping cache flag ->

```
# toggling embedding cache eviction to legacy
redwoodctl config set embeddings.eviction_policy legacy --region eu-west1
```

priya: bumping HPA min replicas for embedding-cache-eu: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment/embedding-cache --replicas=6`

ops-sre: gating gateway concurrency -> applied new config to gateway-ingress configmap, reloaded proxy.

emma-li: rechecking errors after changes — 60s window: 502s down from 4.3% -> 1.2%. Latency also trending down.

devon: still seeing a tail. I'll open a temporary route rule to shift 20% of traffic for non-enterprise customers to eu-west2 until origin queues drain. ops-sre can you push the route?

ops-sre: pushing route rule via control plane now. Command:
```
redwoodctl route shift --from eu-west1 --to eu-west2 --percent 20 --predicate "!tag:enterprise"
```
Applied.

priya: metrics look stable post-route. Origin queue depth falling. 502s now ~0.4% over 2m.

devon: rolling back the cache policy fully to be safe. Will keep the autoscaler bump for the next 30m.

pagerduty: Escalation suspended — issue under active mitigation.

emma-li: quick customer check: messaging support to reach the three affected tenants, offering status and apology. No major revenue-impacting customers impacted.

sam-k: nice work. I'm taking the night oncall handoff at 2276543400. devon/priya — any outstanding tasks I should track?

devon: keep autoscaler min=6 for 30m, monitor origin queue < 5. If 502 > 1% again, revert route shift and open full incident. Also confirm no backend deploys occur in eu-west1 until cool-down.

priya: I'll set alert sticky: origin-queue-depth > 8 in eu-west1 to trigger PD if it resurges.

sam-k: ack. Handoff accepted. I'll check back at +15 and +45. If anything else flares I'll ping oncall. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Note: Incident 3a7f9c marked as mitigated by devon at 2276543378. Will remain in monitoring for 45m then auto-resolve if stable.

devon: closing thread for active mitigation — will reopen if error rate climbs. Thanks all. :heart:
